column1: # The store tree, one line per directory: path, owner, group, mode.
# Tab-separated. setup-tree.sh creates exactly this; check-units.sh walks it.
# No file is pre-created: every file in the tree is written by its one writer
# at run time (heartbeat/*.hb, fault, halt, halts/<writer>, gt/<boot>/*.trace,
# Modes: 0755 is a directory with one writer, its owner. 1775 is a directory
# whose entries have different owners: root owns it, the group may create in
# it, the sticky bit lets an entry be renamed over, unlinked or replaced only
# by the entry's owner (or root). See README "The halts/ slot problem".
# 2750 is the trace root alone, gt:gtring-trace with the setgid bit: the trace names every peer
# that presented a certificate, so the four observers read it through the
# group and no other account reads a byte. See README "The trace root is
# group-readable". The setgid bit makes what ghostunnel creates inside inherit the group; it requests 0750 directories and 0640
# tunnel's store. Root is root:gtobs-tunnel 1775: tunnel creates fault, halt and
# their .tmp here through the group bit and heartbeat/ is its own; sticky stops
# it renaming or removing copy/, copy-super/ and halts/, which it does not own.
# ghostunnel's traces. ghostunnel creates lock, chains/<sha256>.der, <boot>/ and <boot>/<seq>.trace
# inside; never deletes. gt:gtring-trace 2750: gt writes as the owner, the four observers read
# through the group, nobody else lists it or reaches a file in it by name.
